([[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]]) | college = [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]] (2020–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 27 | draft_team = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|start}}–{{nbay|2025|end}} | team1 = [[Brooklyn Nets]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]] | team2 = →[[Long Island Nets]] | highlights = * First-team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] (2021) * SEC All-Freshman Team (2021) | team3 = [[Milwaukee Bucks]] | years3 = {{nbay|2025|end}} }} '''Cameron Bouchea Thomas''' (born October 13, 2001) is an American professional [[basketball]] player who last played for the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He was a consensus [[five-star recruit]] and one of the best [[shooting guards]] in the 2020 class. He is the youngest player in NBA history to score 40+ points in three straight games. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU Tigers]]. ==Early life== Thomas was born in [[Yokosuka]], Kanagawa Prefecture, Japan while his mother was living there. When he was seven, he won a contest by making 33 [[free throw]]s in a row.{{Cite magazine |last=Dellenger |first=Ross |date=March 20, 2021 |title=The Mother-and-Son Bond That Fuels LSU's Cameron Thomas |url=https://www.si.com/college/2021/03/21/cameron-thomas-lsu-mom-march-madness |access-date=2021-10-29 |magazine=Sports Illustrated |language=en-us}} As a freshman, Thomas began playing basketball for [[Oscar F. Smith High School]] in [[Chesapeake, Virginia]].{{cite web |last1=Brown |first1=Mitch |title=Oscar Smith eyeing a state title game return with the help of a fantastic freshman |url=https://www.wtkr.com/2017/02/10/oscar-smith-eyeing-a-state-title-game-return-with-the-help-of-a-fantastic-freshman |publisher=[[WTKR]] |access-date=May 15, 2020 |date=February 10, 2017}} He did not play in his sophomore season because he and his mother "weren't on the same page" as the team's coaching staff.{{cite web |last1=Teel |first1=David |title=Cam Thomas having breakout spring for Boo Williams team |url=https://www.dailypress.com/sports/dp-spt-cam-thomas-eybl-0530-story.html |website=[[Daily Press (Virginia)|Daily Press]] |access-date=May 15, 2020 |date=May 29, 2018}} For his junior season, he transferred to [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] in [[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]], where he joined [[Cole Anthony]] and [[Kofi Cockburn]] in one of the most touted teams in the country.{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=Preseason Top 25 High School Basketball Rankings: No. 2 Oak Hill Academy |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/ihqcMcu7H0SCq-7KRvt4fQ/preseason-top-25-high-school-basketball-rankings--no-2-oak-hill-academy.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=May 15, 2020 |date=October 17, 2018}} Thomas averaged a team-high 26.2 points, 3.8 rebounds and 3.4 assists per game, leading his team to a 31–5 record.{{cite web |last1=Hayes |first1=Tim |title=Thomas, Robinson among the stars for Oak Hill Academy Warriors |url=https://www.heraldcourier.com/sports/thomas-robinson-among-the-stars-for-oak-hill-academy-warriors/article_213f5ccc-f08b-11e9-a0d8-0b27003db54d.html |website=[[Bristol Herald Courier]] |access-date=May 15, 2020 |date=October 16, 2019}}{{cite web |last1=Divens |first1=Jordan |title=2018-19 MaxPreps Boys Basketball Junior All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/Unx8d7lBbEmJkCDKNtEhCw/2018-19-maxpreps-boys-basketball-junior-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=May 15, 2020 |date=April 17, 2019}} In July 2019, he was named Offensive Player of the Year at the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League]] after averaging a league-best 29.5 points per game for Boo Williams.{{cite web |last1=Pope IV |first1=Jonas |title=This five-star NC State basketball target named EYBL Offensive Player of the Year |url=https://www.charlotteobserver.com/sports/college/article232250077.html |website=[[The Charlotte Observer]] |access-date=May 15, 2020 |date=July 3, 2019}} As a senior at Oak Hill, Thomas averaged 31.5 points, six rebounds and 3.4 assists per game. Thomas posted 30-plus points in nine games, including two 40-point performances. He led his team to the Tournament of Champions title, where he was named [[most valuable player]].{{cite web |last1=Raymer |first1=Kai |title=Oak Hill claims fourth Bass Pro Tournament of Champions title |url=https://www.ozarkssportszone.com/2020/01/18/oak-hill-claims-fourth-bass-pro-tournament-of-champions-title/ |publisher=Ozarks Sports Zone |access-date=May 15, 2020 |date=January 18, 2020}} Thomas was selected to play in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]].{{cite magazine |last1=Jordan |first1=Jason |title=Jordan Brand Classic Rosters Revealed |url=https://www.si.com/college/recruiting/basketball/jordan-brand-classic-2020-michael-jordan-chicago-cade-cunningham-jalen-green |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=May 15, 2020 |date=February 14, 2020}} ===Recruiting=== On November 18, 2019, Thomas committed to play [[college basketball]] at [[Louisiana State University]] (LSU). He chose the [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|Tigers]] over an offer from [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], among others, after taking official visits to both schools.{{cite web |last1=Biancardi |first1=Paul |last2=Borzello |first2=Jeff |title=Five-star scorer Cameron Thomas commits to LSU |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/recruiting/basketball/mens/story/_/id/28108481/five-star-scorer-cameron-thomas-commits-lsu |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=May 15, 2020 |date=November 18, 2019}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2020}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Cameron Thomas | position = [[Shooting guard|SG]] | hometown = [[Chesapeake, Virginia|Chesapeake, VA]] | highschool = [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] (VA) | feet = 6 | inches = 3 | weight = 180 | 40 = | commitdate = November 18, 2019 | scout stars = | rivals stars = 5 | 247 stars = 5 | espn stars = 5 | espn grade = 93 }} {{College Athlete Recruit End | 40 = | year = 2020 | rivals ref title = LSU 2020 Basketball Commitments | scout ref title = | espn ref title = 2020 LSU Tigers Recruiting Class | rivals school = lsu | scout s = | espn schoolid = 99 | 247 overall = 25 | rivals overall = 27 | espn overall = 23 | access-date = August 3, 2020 | bball = yes }} ==College career== In Thomas's college debut on November 26, 2020, he scored 27 points in a 94–81 win against [[SIU Edwardsville Cougars men's basketball|SIU Edwardsville]].{{cite news |title=LSU's Thomas scores 27 in collegiate debut |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401262506 |access-date=December 2, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 26, 2020}} Thomas led all freshman in scoring with 23 points per game, while also averaging 3.4 rebounds and 1.4 assists per game. He was named to the First Team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]].{{cite news |last1=Plain |first1=Megan |title=Chesapeake's Cam Thomas declares for NBA Draft after one season at LSU |url=https://www.wtkr.com/sports/chesapeakes-cam-thomas-declares-for-nba-draft-after-one-season-at-lsu |access-date=June 19, 2021 |work=WTKR |date=April 15, 2021}} On April 15, 2021, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]], forgoing his remaining college eligibility.{{cite news |last1=Guilbeau |first1=Glenn |title=LSU star Cameron Thomas declares for NBA Draft; Jalen Cook, Aundre Hyatt may transfer |url=https://www.theadvertiser.com/story/sports/college/lsu/2021/04/15/lsu-basketball-nba-draft-cameron-thomas/7218794002/ |access-date=June 19, 2021 |work=[[The Daily Advertiser (Lafayette, Louisiana)|The Daily Advertiser]] |date=April 15, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Brooklyn Nets (2021–2026)=== ==== 2021–22 season ==== Thomas was selected with the 27th pick in the [[2021 NBA draft]] by the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite news |last1=Winfield |first1=Kristian |title=Nets pick up LSU guard Cameron Thomas at No. 27 overall |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/sports/basketball/nets/ny-nets-draft-cameron-thomas-20210730-6yjm6bh435aybcv3nm7i4jbaei-story.html |access-date=July 31, 2021 |work=[[New York Daily News]] |date=July 29, 2021}} Thomas was later included in the roster of the Nets to play in [[2021 NBA Summer League]].{{cite web|title=Brooklyn Nets announce summer League roster|url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/08/03/brooklyn-nets-announce-summer-league-roster|date=August 3, 2021|website=nba.com|access-date=August 6, 2021}} On August 5, 2021, Thomas signed with the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Sign Cam Thomas |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/2021/08/05/brooklyn-nets-sign-cam-thomas |website=nba.com |access-date=6 August 2021}} Thomas was named [[NBA Summer League]] MVP with [[Davion Mitchell]] averaging 27 points per game and was the Summer League leading scorer, and was named to the Summer League First Team.{{Cite web|last=Conway|first=Tyler|title=Kings' Davion Mitchell, Nets' Cameron Thomas Named Co-MVPs of 2021 NBA Summer League|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/10010571-kings-davion-mitchell-nets-cameron-thomas-named-co-mvps-of-2021-nba-summer-league|access-date=2021-08-18|website=Bleacher Report|language=en}} On October 19, Thomas made his debut in the [[National Basketball Association|NBA]], coming off the bench to score two points in a 104–127 loss to the [[2021–22 Milwaukee Bucks season|Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite web|title=Bucks begin title defense with 127-104 victory over Nets|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap/_/gameId/401358773|date=October 19, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=October 19, 2021}} On November 20, while on assignment with the [[Long Island Nets]], he scored 46 points in a 114–110 win over the [[Raptors 905]].{{Cite web |last=Taylor |first=Cody |date=November 21, 2021 |title=Nets' Cam Thomas erupted for 46 points in G League assignment |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2021/11/21/nets-cam-thomas-erupted-for-46-points-in-g-league-assignment/ |access-date=November 22, 2021 |website=Rookie Wire|publisher=USA Today}} ==== 2022–23 season ==== Thomas joined the Nets' [[2022 NBA Summer League]] roster.{{Cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets 2022 NBA2K23 Summer League Roster {{!}} NBA.com |url=https://www.nba.com/summer-league/2022/vegas/team/1610612751/nets |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=www.nba.com}} On July 18, 2022, Thomas was named to the All-NBA Summer League First Team.{{Cite web |last=Darro |first=Thomas |date=2022-07-18 |title=Brooklyn Nets Guard Receives Impressive Offseason Award |url=https://heavy.com/sports/brooklyn-nets/brooklyn-nets-guard-receives-impressive-offseason-award/ |access-date=2022-07-21 |website=Heavy.com |language=en-US}} On December 10, Thomas scored a then-career-high 33 points in a 136–133 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nets-news-no-kevin-durant-or-kyrie-irving-no-problem-as-cam-thomas-drops-career-high|title=No Kevin Durant or Kyrie Irving, no problem as Cam Thomas drops career-high|website=ClutchPoints|last=Yapkowitz|first=David|date=December 10, 2022|access-date=December 10, 2022}} On February 4, 2023, Thomas put up a then career-high 44 points in a 125–123 win over the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nets-news-cam-thomas-shows-brooklyn-he-deserves-more-minutes-after-44-point-explosion|title=Cam Thomas shows Nets he deserves more minutes after 44-point explosion|website=ClutchPoints|last=Guinhawa|first=Angelo|date=February 4, 2023|access-date=February 4, 2023}} The next game, Thomas scored a new career-high 47 points in a 124–116 loss to the [[Los Angeles Clippers]]. He became the second youngest player in NBA history to score at least 40 points in consecutive games, behind [[LeBron James]]. On February 7, 2023, Thomas put up 43 points in a 116–112 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]]. With this game, Thomas became the youngest player in NBA history to score at least 40 points in three consecutive games.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nets-news-no-kyrie-irving-no-problem-cam-thomas-explodes-vs-clippers|title=No Kyrie Irving, no problem: Nets' Cam Thomas enters LeBron James territory after explosion vs. Clippers|website=ClutchPoints|last=Songco|first=Paolo|date=February 6, 2023|access-date=February 6, 2023}} On February 10, 2023, he was fined $40,000 by the NBA for saying "[[no homo]]", which was perceived as anti-gay, during a post-game interview following a game the night before against the [[Chicago Bulls]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/35631269/cam-thomas-fined-40k-anti-gay-remark-interview|title=Cam Thomas fined $40K for anti-gay remark during interview|website=ESPN.com|date=February 10, 2023|access-date=February 10, 2023}} ==== 2023–24 season ==== On October 25, 2023, Thomas put up 36 points off the bench in a 114–113 loss to the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]]. His 36 points were the most off the bench in a season-opener in NBA history.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nets-news-cam-thomas-makes-nba-history-with-36-point-explosion-in-brooklyns-season-opening-loss-to-cavs|title=Nets' Cam Thomas makes NBA history with 36-point explosion in Brooklyn's season-opening loss to Cavs|website=ClutchPoints|last=Meyer|first=Nick|date=October 25, 2023|access-date=October 25, 2023}} On November 6, Thomas scored a season-high 45 points during a 129–125 loss to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{cite magazine|url=https://www.si.com/nba/nets/gameday/nets-fall-short-against-the-bucks-despite-cam-thomas-45-point-night- |title= Nets fall short against the Bucks despite Cam Thomas' 45-point night|magazine=Sports Illustrated|last=Sunjic|first=Peter|date=November 6, 2023|access-date=November 6, 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231107103055/https://www.si.com/nba/nets/gameday/nets-fall-short-against-the-bucks-despite-cam-thomas-45-point-night- |archive-date=November 7, 2023 |url-status=dead}} On December 16, Thomas put up 41 points in a 124–120 loss to the [[Golden State Warriors]]. He also surpassed [[Bernard King]]'s record for the most 40-point games in Nets history at age 22 years old or younger with his sixth career 40-point game.{{cite web|url=https://clutchpoints.com/nets-news-cam-thomas-breaks-out-shooting-slump-record-setting-performance|title=Nets' Cam Thomas reacts to breaking out of slump with record-setting performance|website=ClutchPoints|last=Slater|first=Erik|date=December 18, 2023|access-date=December 19, 2023}} ==== 2024–25 season ==== Thomas made 25 appearances (23 starts) for Brooklyn during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 24.0 points, 3.3 rebounds, and 3.8 assists. On March 15, 2025, Thomas was ruled out for the remainder of the season due to a left hamstring strain.{{Cite web |date=March 15, 2025 |title=Nets' Cam Thomas (hamstring) expected to be out for season |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/44265452/nets-cam-thomas-hamstring-expected-season |access-date=March 17, 2025 |website=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press |language=en}} ==== 2025–26 season ==== On September 4, 2025, Thomas signed a one-year, $6 million qualifying offer deal to return to the Nets after a summer spent in restricted free agency.{{Cite web |last=Vorkunov |first=Mike |date=September 5, 2025 |title=Cam Thomas is betting on himself with a one-year Nets deal. Will it pay off? |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/6598481/2025/09/05/cam-thomas-nets-signing-free-agency/ |access-date=December 3, 2025 |website=[[The New York Times]]}} He made 24 appearances (eight starts) for Brooklyn during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], averaging 15.6 points, 1.8 rebounds, and 3.1 assists. On February 5, 2026, Thomas was waived by the Nets following the acquisition of [[Josh Minott]].{{Cite web |title=Brooklyn Nets Acquire Josh Minott |url=https://www.nba.com/nets/news/brooklynnetsacquirejoshminott |quote= In a related transaction, the Nets have requested waivers on guard Cam Thomas.|access-date=2026-02-06 |date=2026-02-05 |website=NBA.com |language=en}} === Milwaukee Bucks (2026) === On February 8, 2026, Thomas signed with the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].{{Cite web |title=Milwaukee Bucks Sign Cam Thomas {{!}} Milwaukee Bucks |url=https://bucks.com/news/milwaukee-bucks-sign-cam-thomas |access-date=2026-02-09 |website=bucks.com |language=en}} On February 9, against the [[2025–26 Orlando Magic season|Orlando Magic]], Thomas made his debut, tallying up 4 points, one rebound, and one assist in 13 minutes of gameplay. On February 11, Thomas came off the bench, tallying 34 points (12-20 FG, 4-6 3PT, 6-6 FT), four rebounds, and two assists over 25 minutes in a 116–108 victory over the Magic. Thomas tied the record of scoring the most points by a Bucks reserve in a regular season game since [[Jordan Nwora]] in 2021.{{cite web |last=RotoWire Staff |title=Bucks' Cam Thomas: Scores 34 points with four treys |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/bucks-cam-thomas-scores-34-points-with-four-treys/ |website=[[CBS Sports]] |publisher=Paramount |date=February 11, 2026 |access-date=February 11, 2026 }} On March 23, the Bucks waived Thomas.{{cite web |title=Bucks Waive Cam Thomas |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/48292059/bucks-waive-guard-cam-thomas-convert-pete-nance-contract |website=[[ESPN]] |publisher=ESPN |date=March 23, 2026 |access-date=March 23, 2026 }}
